items.title: Implement boundary agreement: case runner, slice --cases, done-check by cases
items.description: Build steps 1 to 3 of the T-32 design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-boundary-agreement-design.md) by the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-21-boundary-agreement.md, on branch boundary-agreement (design and plan are committed there). Six tasks: groundwork in eval/flow/sources; the PM's expected values with the shop fixture; team segments and finding each team's own flow; running the cases (isolated and end to end, rejects); slice --cases with the docs on what a pin means; requirements closing Compute and Send items by cases, then an Acme sandbox replay. Before starting, ask the developer: (1) confirm the plan's two decisions beyond the design: teams with sheets but no own flow fall back to the T-30 rule-text check; Receive and Carry stay structural; (2) execution method: subagent-driven (recommended) or native. The editor's Requirements panel (design section 6) is a separate, later plan.

items.title: Test middleware: dsheets drives the team's code through a team-supplied adapter
items.description: From the T-32 brainstorm, 2026-11-21; developer's pick to do right after T-32. Today verify needs the team's tests to run every case and write results.json. Wanted instead: dsheets builds each case's request from cases.toml and the input interface; the team supplies only an adapter saying how to reach its code (HTTP URL, CLI command, produce to a topic, or a unit-level entry point). The adapter also has to say how to fix inputs that are not on the wire (context such as request time, config, test database rows), how to stand in for calls made on the way (record the request the code sends, compare with expected_calls, return the response the case gives, so another team's environment is never needed), and how to collect outputs that are not a response (a message produced to a topic). dsheets then keeps only the fields the sheet declares (verify already ignores undeclared fields such as traceId) and records evidence as verify does.

items.title: Brainstorm: help an owner update their sheet, flow and schema after a requirements change
items.description: Brainstorming session, to be picked after T-26 and its dependency T-29 are complete. Source: the T-27 Acme walkthrough (acme-corp/WALKTHROUGH.md, steps 9 to 14), where the Orders developer took the --apply branch and then had to do a lot of manual work, in the right order, to bring their own files in line with the flow change: unpin free_shipping in their flow (flow editor first, or the flow breaks, see T-31); change the row from derived to input in the sheet editor; add the field to the .avsc by hand (the editor does not edit source schemas); remove the stale computes entry; run validate and slice; commit; merge. Cart's developer did the mirror image: add the row and its table, fix a typo the editor let through (T-28), pin it, check, merge. Questions for the session: should --apply (or a companion command) also update the owner's own sheet and flow where the requirement says exactly what to do (Compute added or removed, Receive, Send), or only suggest the edits; how to keep the order of edits right; whether the source schema (avsc, OpenAPI, JSON Schema) should be edited too; whether the editors should offer these steps from a requirement (open the row, pre-fill the change); how this relates to T-30, where Compute, Send and Receive never close from the owners' work. Related: T-28, T-30, T-31, D-18 to D-20. Nothing is decided.

items.title: Let derived and sent rows declare a type, so a mistyped table result like "False" is caught
items.description: Found in the T-27 Acme sandbox, 2026-11-14, while the developer built a Cart table row in the visual editor: the last rule's result was typed as False and saved as the string "False", not the boolean false. validate reported 0 errors and 0 warnings, so Cart would have sent text where order-placed needs a boolean. Cause: a derived row, and the send on it, cannot declare a type (type is rejected on derived rows with derived-input-key), so nothing says what the table's results should be. Wanted: a way to set the type on a derived row or its send (boolean, number, string), with validate and the editor checking table results, formula results and lookup values against it, so a wrong-case or wrong-type cell is caught. Related: the same gap is why requirements --apply refuses with 'type unknown' for a ternary formula, and its error message advises giving the row a type, which the format does not allow.

items.title: Flow and sheet editors: editing the sheet first leaves a flow the editor cannot open, with no hint about order
items.description: Found in the T-27 Acme walkthrough, 2026-11-14. In the Orders repo, turning free_shipping into an input in the sheet editor first made flow.toml invalid (computes names an input row), so the flow editor refused to draw it with 'fix it by hand first' and the unpin it was needed for could not be done there. The working order is flow editor first (unpin), then sheet editor. Each editor handles one file, and nothing says a change spanning sheet and flow needs an order. Options: when the sheet editor turns a pinned derived row into an input (or deletes a pinned row), warn that the flow pins it, or offer to remove the pin on save; or let the flow editor open an invalid flow read-only with the offending line and a one-click fix. Developer, 2026-11-15: deferred until after T-32, since the T-32 brainstorm may change how the editors and --apply handle edit order.

needs_review.reason: T-32 design: section 6 (requirement-driven editing) saves a team's sheet and flow together, which is meant to remove the edit-order problem; T-31 may become unnecessary or shrink.

items.title: dsheets diff: default base prefers the registry's followed branch
items.description: Per D-17 (resolved 2026-11-13): resolve diff's default base from the branch the registry follows, as dsheets impact does, falling back to the git chain (origin/HEAD, origin/main, origin/master, main, master) when there is no registry. diff and impact must never disagree about the base. Update docs/diff.md and add tests for both paths.

items.title: Turn a sheet change into implementation work per team
items.description: From 'Related work' in the visual-editor spec. Turn the difference between the committed files and the edited ones (sheets, flows, interfaces) into requirements for whoever implements them: per team, what to compute, send, carry or add to a schema. Works whether the change came from the editor, an LLM or a hand edit, which is why it is not part of the editor. Built on the structured changes from T-5's `dsheets diff` and the revision-aware reader T-5 adds to internal/store (store.Committed alone only reads HEAD). Git-native, no CI-platform dependency. Developer decisions 2026-11-11: brainstorm in its own session, after T-5; effects on other teams' consumers of a changed field belong here, not in T-5.

items.title: Row-level diffs for pull requests
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 8. Git-native `dsheets diff [base]..[head]`: reads both revisions from git, no CI-platform API; markdown/text on stdout plus --json. Default base is origin/HEAD (fallbacks origin/main, origin/master, local main/master; else error), compared at the merge-base; share one base resolver with internal/impact (open: registry-followed branch first). Needs a NEW revision-aware reader in internal/store: store.Committed only reads HEAD, so it cannot be reused as-is. Sheets first, flows (boundary and interface differences, per team = the repo being diffed) in the same PR; git diff driver (.gitattributes, scoped narrowly, never *.toml) comes after the diff works. Rows matched by id; added/removed rows listed individually, including whole added or deleted sheet folders. Changed rows show before/after for formula, source, type, send. Logic changes only by default; --all adds label/style changes; --cases adds cases.toml; CSVs never included. Always exits 0 unless there is an error. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-row-level-diff-design.md. Shares the comparison with T-6.

items.title: Editor M3: decision tables, lookups and live case preview
items.description: Milestone 3 of the visual editor. Decision-table grid: columns from rows you pick; cells take conditions such as `>= 2`, `-` or values; add, remove and reorder rules and condition columns; choose the hit policy; gaps and overlaps flagged while editing. Lookup form: `from` and `key`; inline `values` editable; values from a CSV values_file shown read-only with the file's path. Switching rule kind warns before discarding the old rule. Live preview: when typing pauses, run cases.Generate on the in-memory draft and show every case's result (or why there is none, such as 'rejected earlier') using the eval engine; the row's grid dots, rule and send column update before saving. Read-only view (D-12, first PR): the sheet page shows every decision table as a rule table (one row per rule, one column per input, result column, hit policy), the same shape the editor edits. Remove the 2-input cross-tab (grid2D in internal/render/rule.go) and the 1-input inline list.

items.title: Editor M4: flow panel and interface re-import merges
items.description: Milestone 4 of the visual editor. Flow page with review marks always on. Panel for a value row: 'compute here' on every possible step pins it (writes computes or callee_computes); unpinning returns it to automatic placement. For each mark on an interface file in this repository: add field (name, type, required) or map to an existing field (writes carries). Interfaces reached through an alias: source are read-only. Adding a field to an imported interface warns and writes `local = true`. '+ stage' between columns and stage editing (kind, interfaces, producer, caller, callee). Serving a flow with --edit also makes its end-to-end sheet editable when that sheet is in this repository. Change `dsheets interface import` to merge when the file exists: keep `local = true` fields absent from the schema, drop the mark once the schema has the field, print the fields kept; add `local` to schema/interface.schema.json and docs/flows.md.

items.title: Editor: open a sheet that has validation errors so it can be repaired
items.description: Today a sheet with validation errors cannot be served, so `serve --edit` cannot open it and it cannot be repaired in the editor (noted in the T-17 and T-18/T-20 handoffs). Serve it anyway with the errors shown, and let the editor fix them.

items.title: Editor: the Uses row IDs in the panel look like links but do nothing
items.description: Developer feedback on the M2 editor (2026-11-06): in the panel, the row IDs under Uses are blue and underlined, like links, but clicking them does nothing. Either make them act (open that row in the panel, scroll it into view) or stop styling them as links.

items.title: Validator: an input row's reject may name only itself and other inputs (D-9)
items.description: Per D-9 (2026-11-08). The validator rejects an input row's [[row.reject]] whose `when` names a derived row. Error message points the author to the fix, e.g. 'input weight_kg: reject names derived row zone; move this check to a reject on a derived row'. An input's `when` keeps allowing any row. Update docs/format.md (Expressions section, line ~176, and the [[row.reject]] table row) and add a validator test. The editor's reject form (T-3/T-4) should offer only the row itself and inputs for an input's reject. No existing sheet is affected (no input rejects in specs/ or examples/).

items.title: Editor: save from the panel, and show an edited or new row on the sheet before saving
items.description: Developer feedback on the M2 editor (2026-11-06): adding or editing a row only shows on the sheet after a whole-sheet Save from the bottom bar. Wanted: a Save in the panel itself. Related: T-3's live preview would redraw the row's grid dots, rule and send column from the in-memory draft before saving.

items.title: Allow reject conditions on input rows
items.description: Decision D-8 (developer, 2026-11-07): input rows may have [[row.reject]]. Today the validator refuses them (reject-on-input in internal/validate/validate.go) and docs/format.md lists rejects for derived rows only; the rule dates from the first commit with no recorded reason. Change: drop the reject-on-input check; a reject on an input row may refer to the row itself and to the inputs named in its when; update docs/format.md (field table and expressions section) and schema/sheet.schema.json descriptions; make sure graph dependencies, eval (when an input's reject is evaluated), cases generation (row:reject:CODE targets) and the rendered page handle rejects on inputs. The M2 editor already offers Add reject on every row, so it needs no change beyond testing it. Raised while testing the M2 editor.

items.title: Editor M1: comment-preserving TOML writer and file store
items.description: First write the implementation plan for the whole visual editor from the agreed spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-visual-editor-design.md (no plan exists yet; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-cross-repo-references.md is the pattern). Then build milestone 1, with no UI. (a) A file store interface: load a file with a token identifying its version, save only if the token still matches, and answer 'the version in the last commit'; nothing else in the editor touches the filesystem. (b) A span-level TOML writer built on internal/sheet/positions.go: each row, stage, interface field and top-level key is a span of lines; replace only changed spans, insert new ones, remove deleted ones. Changed spans are written in canonical form (key order and alignment of specs/order-checkout/sheet.toml, sub-tables indented two spaces). A comment block directly above a row moves and is deleted with it; section comments stay put; comments inside a changed span are kept where their key still exists. go-toml/v2 drops comments, so it cannot write. Done when every example sheet, flow and interface round-trips byte-for-byte when nothing changed, and edits change only the expected spans.

items.title: Editor M2: sheet editing (inputs, formulas, sends, rejects) and save
items.description: Milestone 2 of the visual editor (spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-visual-editor-design.md; plan tasks 5-9 in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-06-visual-editor.md). FIRST STEP (developer's call, 2026-11-06 concierge): an independent review of milestone 1 (internal/store and internal/tomledit, merge 9c5c18a), e.g. /code-review, because it was only self-reviewed; fixes land on the T-2 branch before Task 5. Then: `dsheets serve --edit`; serve stays read-only without the flag. Side panel on the sheet page: name, ID (locked after first save), description; rule kinds Input (source, type, usage, when, default), Formula (CEL, suggestions for rows and functions, `uses` filled from the formula, rows that would make a cycle not offered) and Text; sends including call sends (send.target); rejects; open questions; one-click 'add it as a request input' for names that are not rows yet. Unsaved-changes bar with Save and Discard; closing the tab with unsaved edits asks first. Save pipeline per the spec's 'Saving' section: conflict check through the store token; refuse only errors the edit introduces (compared by code, row and message); raise version by one at most once per commit; write; regenerate cases as `dsheets cases` does (cases.Preserve, the reference time already in cases.toml) and report the summary.

items.title: Formatter and pre-commit hook
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 7. Canonical formatting (`dsheets fmt` or a taplo fmt configuration) and a pre-commit hook. Should be cheap once T-1's canonical span writer exists: reuse its canonical layout so the editor and the formatter never disagree.

items.title: Lists: derive or send one value per item
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 3; an open question from the original handoff. Arrays import as a single `array` field, and there is no way to derive or send one value per item. Likely shape: a group of rows with a shared 'for each' label, as tax forms handle repeated dependents. Needs a design conversation. It changes sheet.toml, so the editor's forms (T-2 to T-4) would have to cover it; T-1 works on line spans and does not depend on it.

items.title: Evidence per piece and per team in flows
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 2. Evidence is recorded per sheet. There is no view of evidence per piece or per team inside a flow, or in the combined grid.

items.title: Draft rows from natural language with an LLM
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 9 (Phase 2 of the original handoff). Ambiguities must become open_questions, never guesses.

items.title: DMN XML export
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 10 (Phase 2). Export only, never execution, for viewing in existing DMN tools. Only matters if FEEL or DMN tooling becomes important; CEL stays the expression language until then.

items.title: Draft sheets from existing code
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 11 (Phase 3: documenting existing code without changing it). An LLM proposes sheets from existing code, including SQL strings and config keys.

items.title: Production evidence from OpenTelemetry traces
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 12 (Phase 3). Configured at the process level, with payloads redacted before storage. The evidence model already has a `trace` run kind and internal/evidence.Store is an interface; nothing ingests traces yet.

items.title: Scheduled database and config snapshots with diffs
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 13 (Phase 3). Snapshots on a schedule, with a diff view between snapshots.

items.title: Replay captured requests through the evaluator
items.description: BACKLOG.md item 14 (Phase 3). Replay captured requests through the evaluator and compare with the payloads actually sent, to verify inferred rows.

items.title: Sheet page: keep the column header (row numbers of the grid) visible while scrolling
items.description: Developer feedback on the M2 editor (2026-11-06): the table header with the grid's line numbers should be sticky on scroll. Applies to the sheet page in general, not only serve --edit; check print and the phone layout (the table scrolls sideways there).

items.title: Editor polish: header at 390px, scroll new rows into view, stale dots on cycles
items.description: Small editor glitches from past handoffs, bundled into one task: (1) at 390px, following a Uses link can push the sheet's column header off the top (the table box sits partly above the window); (2) a newly added row isn't scrolled into view when first drawn (`reveal` in editor.js can do it; offered in T-17); (3) a formula edit that creates a cycle briefly draws grid dots from the last good evaluation.

items.title: Lookups: design-time values as an editable table in sheet.toml, not CSV files
items.description: Developer, 2026-11-08: values_file CSVs are an outlier. In real code the lookup data lives in a database, so a CSV in the repo adds little; a table-style input in the editor, like the decision-table grid, should be enough. Today inline values take one key only ({ Gold = 0.10 }), so multi-key lookups such as shipping_fee (zone, shipping_method, weight_kg, with ranges like (1..5]) need a CSV. Needs: an inline multi-key form in sheet.toml (for example columns + rows, as [row.table] has, with the lookup cell grammar including ranges); loader, validator (overlaps and gaps), eval and cases support; the panel's lookup values edited in a grid reusing the decision-table grid; docs/format.md and schema/sheet.schema.json; migrating specs/order-checkout (zone, shipping_fee) and examples/pieces. Whether values_file stays is D-14. Raised while building T-3's lookup form (branch editor-m3-lookups), which shows values_file data read-only.

items.title: Git diff driver for row-level diffs (.gitattributes)
items.description: Developer, 2026-11-11: do after dsheets diff exists (T-5, merged in PR #13). A diff driver so plain git diff and git log -p show row-level changes locally. Scope by filename or folder (sheet.toml, flow.toml, or a .gitattributes inside the specs folder), never *.toml, since dsheets files live next to application code. Fall back to the plain text diff for any file it cannot parse or when dsheets is not installed. Web PR views do not use it; docs/diff.md notes it as later.

items.title: Build `dsheets requirements`: per-team requirements from a flow change
items.description: Build `dsheets requirements <flow>`, per the design in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-13-requirements-design.md (decisions D-18 to D-20): compare flow.Analyze at base and head and list Compute, Send, Receive, Carry and Schema requirements per team, with stable ids, why, and needs links, ordered by dependency; `--apply` edits interfaces on new branches in each owner repo (--no-push, --branch, --change). Dev is done. Status stays in_progress: it closes, and its PR merges, only after T-27 sandbox testing and the fixes it turns up are applied here.

items.title: Set up a dummy Acme Corp: several team repos, each with dsheets, plus a registry
items.description:
Testing sandbox for the multi-repo features (T-26 `dsheets requirements` and its --apply, registry, impact, slice, flow checks). Build a fictional Acme Corp OUTSIDE this repo (e.g. D:/projects/acme-corp/) as real git repos, so fetches, branches and pushes behave as they do for a real org.

Scope:
- 3-4 team repos (e.g. cart, payments, shipping, notifications; generic order-checkout style, no industry jargon), each with its own dsheets folder: sheet.toml files, interfaces (OpenAPI/Avro/JSON Schema), a dsheets.toml, and a few deliberately tricky cases (a handoff and a call stage, a carried field, a lookup).
- One flow repo or folder holding the end-to-end flow across the teams.
- A registry repo whose .gitmodules lists every team repo (url, branch, dsheets folder), following main.
- Remotes: local bare repos (file:// or paths) acting as origin for each repo so `--apply` can clone, branch and push without touching a hosted service. A small script (or README) that recreates the whole setup from scratch and resets it between test runs.
- Test scenarios written down: a flow change that adds a field a consumer needs, a producer change that breaks a consumer (`dsheets impact`), and a `requirements --apply` run that opens interface-edit branches in several repos.

Done when: `dsheets requirements`, `--apply`, `impact` and `slice` all run against the sandbox end to end and the scenarios and reset script are recorded in its README. This task does not change dsheets code; bugs found become new backlog items.

items.title: requirements --apply fails with the default (working-tree) head: fetched sources are mistaken for the flow repo's own files
items.description: FIXED 2026-11-14 on branch requirements (uncommitted): locate() in internal/requirements/run.go no longer treats files under <repo>/.dsheets/sources as files of the flow's own repo. Test: TestRunSchemaFileOfAFetchedSource in internal/requirements/run_test.go (failed before, passes now); full go test ./... green; retested in the Acme sandbox with requirements --apply and no range (Schema items now owned by cart and orders, repo-relative paths, both branches made). Original report: requirements --apply failed with 'product: reading .dsheets/sources/cart-.../checkout-request.toml ... does not exist in HEAD' because the fetched copies sit inside the working tree.

items.title: requirements never empties from the teams' work: only Schema items close, the docs say empty means the flow can merge
items.description: DONE 2026-11-14 on branch requirements (committed locally, not pushed, PR not merged): requirements now closes Compute, Send, Receive and Carry items from the owners' own sheets on the registry-followed branch. States: done (hidden, counted), open, undocumented (own heading, never blocks). Send/Receive match at their boundary and source; the rule comparison covers every non-label field; the flow's own repository and unreadable sheets are never evidence; the rule travels with Compute items; flags --no-check and --show-done; registry team key. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-requirements-done-check-design.md; plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-14-requirements-done-check.md. Verified: go test ./... green (18 packages), Acme sandbox replay closes all four items before the flow merges. Deferred minors: registry fetch error worded as a missing team; unknown hit policy prints as unique; --no-check output differs slightly from before; the N of M count shrinks as Schema items vanish.

items.title: Hand-written PM examples kept alongside generated cases
items.description: From the T-32 brainstorm, 2026-11-21. cases.toml is generated from a sheet's rules, so a PM who writes a row only in English (a text rule) gets no case that exercises it: a text row has no branches, and today no case can be added by hand. Wanted: the PM can write their own examples (for instance 'Silver, subtotal 60: shippingCost 4'), kept next to the generated cases and not overwritten when cases.toml is regenerated, so intent written in English can still be pinned down and checked (including by the chained boundary check proposed in T-32).

items.title: cases.Generate drops a branch when a row has a mapped send
items.description: Found while building T-35, 2026-11-21. In the agree shop fixture, giving the PM's tier row a send with map (Silver = SLV, Standard = STD) made the generator stop emitting a member=true case, so the generated cases covered only one tier. The case-based done-check (T-35) can only be as complete as the generated cases, so a missing branch means an item can close without that branch ever being checked. Investigate why the mapped send changes generation (internal/cases), and make both branches appear.
